---
applyTo: "src/apps/pinch/**"
---

# Pinch rules

Applies on top of CLAUDE.md to everything under `src/apps/pinch/`. Keep the other copy of this file identical in body.

- **Theme: a warm kitchen, quietly.** Surfaces are paper-warm (cream by day, warm black by night) with hairline borders, and a soft shadow only where something floats (the nav pill, a popover, a sheet). Buttons are espresso-ink filled (`--color-primary`) for the one action on a screen and see-through with a hairline for the rest; never a block of orange. Warmth comes from peach tints (`bg-accent`, `--pinch-drizzle-soft`) on groups, fact chips, selected pills and the cards that need a nudge of attention, and from orange as the accent: the today dot and the Week's "Today" pill (`--pinch-drizzle-fill` with `--pinch-drizzle-fill-foreground`, the only places text sits on the orange), a selected outline and ring, the active tab icon, the default price's star, the dashed "New" pills. A screen still reads clean: tint a few things, not everything. The palette, radii, hairlines and field inset live in `pinch.css` as tokens on `html.pinch-theme`, switched on by `usePinchTheme()` while the app is mounted so portaled modals and drawers match. Change the look there, not per component, use semantic tokens (`bg-primary`, `bg-accent`) and the drizzle variable (`text-[var(--pinch-drizzle)]`) rather than raw colors, and body and row text stays the normal color (the tertiary-button rule in `pinch.css`). The app icon and banner follow the other apps: a black tile or banner, the white mark and name, and "Moondreams Dev" in grey.
- **Shape language.** Corners are set by the raised `--radius-*` tokens, so don't hand-roll radii. Options a person picks among are `Pill`s, never radios or a tab strip; an option is a hairline pill and the selected one gets a drizzle outline so its emoji stays readable. Navigation is a floating pill at the bottom of a phone, as wide as its four tabs and never stretched across the screen (Calendar, Recipes, Kitchen, Shopping: `PinchNav`, each tab 64px wide at least and 10px of side padding below `sm` so all four fit 320px on one line), and the same tabs stand in a rail on the left edge from `lg` up. The Shopping tab shows the count left to buy as a small `bg-primary` badge on its icon (only above zero, "99+" past 99) read by its own tiny component, so a tick never re-renders the nav. A later feature joins the tab it belongs to (the fridge and freezer and, later, ingredient stock to Kitchen) and is not a fifth tab. A tick is a circle: every checkbox is a ring until ticked and then filled with the ink, with the tick in the ink's foreground, from one rule on `html.pinch-theme` (`button[role='checkbox']`), never a square, and with a 40×40 target; a done mark is the shared `TickMark`, never ✅ (a square box): the ink circle for a single done row (a planned meal's Cooked, the recipe's Cooked row, cooking mode's record card) and `variant='soft'` (the accent fill, an ink tick, a hairline that survives dark) for a mark that repeats down a list (Week rows, the day drawer's meals). A door to another screen is a rounded tile with a chevron (`EntryTile`), never a pill under a search.
- **Wide screens use the width, not a stretched phone.** The calendar's cells show meal emoji chips on a soft tint of the meal's colour below `lg` and, from `lg`, Google-Calendar-style pills with the meal's truncated title; Week is an agenda from today below `lg` and seven Sunday-to-Saturday columns from `lg`; Recipes, Kitchen and Shopping run in two columns from `lg`. The phone layout is unchanged. Check a new screen at 1280px as well as 390px.
- **The calendar is Month and Week, with a Today button, and a day is its drawer.** The switch is a thin `PillGroup` in `PeriodSwitcher`, the arrows step by the view's unit, and Today appears only while today is outside the shown period. Below `lg` the calendar opens on Week, seven days from today ("Today" as an orange pill, "Tomorrow", then the date; each day's label opens its drawer; there is no "+" per day: planning on a day is the drawer's "Plan on this day", and a day's drawer carries its own Total tile with its other stats following Show stats), with this week's passed days folded under one "Earlier, Oct 11–14" row (their dates); from `lg` it opens on Month and the week is Sunday-to-Saturday columns. The last view picked is remembered per person on the device and a `?view=` link wins. The front volunteers one summary line about the shown period ("This week · 14 meals · $4.10 so far ⚠ ›", absent while nothing is planned in it, nothing at all on a first run but one sentence and "Add your first recipe", with no Plan button or eye in the header until there is a recipe or a saved meal) and, with View options' "Show stats" (off to start), a row of tiles under it (`StatsTiles`: Total, Avg per fully priced meal from three of them, Per g protein, fully priced (the same base) while protein is on, then the daily nutrition switched on as `MacroStats` tiles; a tile with nothing to say isn't drawn, the tiles share one height, their labels wrap and their numbers step down together, and a tap anywhere on them opens the summary sheet through a target behind them); while the Total tile shows, the line keeps only the period and count ("This week · 21 meals ›"), both worded by `getPeriodCostTile`. Every figure (cost and how much is priced, each day's cost opening its day, the averages while the tiles are off, the period's one nudge) lives in the summary sheet behind the line. The cost adds up the planned meals of that period, ahead of today as well as behind it, so it is a cost and never "Spent". A month cell shows dinner first; Week rows show the soft round tick once cooked. A fixed past day's cost tile reads "$0.15+" when it leaves something out, and a period's total takes its qualifier from `getGapQualifier`: "so far" only while a gap can still be priced, "+" once every gap is on a fixed day (a passed week reads "$1,805+"); its averages are over fully priced meals only and need none. A view that reaches past the loaded month window moves the listener's window; paging inside it never does.

- **Emoji carry meaning.** Meals are 🍳 breakfast, 🥪 lunch, 🍝 dinner, 🍿 snack, 🍰 dessert, 🥤 drink, in that order; the same six colors are the `--pinch-meal-*` tokens (and their `-soft` tints behind the calendar's chips and pills). Calories and macros are 🔥 calories (whole numbers), 💪 protein, 🌾 carbs and 🥑 fat in grams, everywhere they appear, through the shared `MacroStats` and its one emoji map `MACRO_EMOJIS` (inline in a row, tiles in a summary, `isCompact` tiles where space is tight), never a sentence of figures. A recipe's facts are one plain muted line of words (`FactsLine`: servings · total time · cost per serving), never pills; the emoji of a drawer's rows sit in a fixed icon column (🥛 fridge, ❄️ freezer, 📝 note); "cooked" is the round `TickMark`, never ✅ or a meal's emoji (🍳 is breakfast). Ingredients have no icon for now (the approach is being rethought), so a row is its name; never a sparkle for "other".
- **One word, one concept (the Pinch glossary).** A "meal" is a slot on a day (breakfast, lunch, dinner…); the reusable plate is a **saved meal** (the pill is "Saved meals", its header action "New saved meal" beside Recipes' "New recipe" and Ideas' "New idea", one shape from `RECIPES_VIEW_NEW_LABELS`, the planned meal's More row "Save to Saved meals"; an unnamed plate is named by its items through the one helper `getPlateTitle` (`utils/mealFormat.ts`, read by the calendar, the plan builder, the Meals sheet and cooking mode): "A & B", "A, B and C", past three "A, B and 2 more", and "A & 2 more" once a name runs past 30 characters, "N more" never split across lines and never "+1"; recording a cook is "Mark as cooked" wherever it is offered); the fridge and freezer list is **Fridge & freezer** in words (never "Prepared meals" or "container" in copy; the code names stay); "note" means only the recipe journal (the price nudge's close is "Not now"); "Got it" is the Shopping half and a help tip's own button, so the Shopping screen's tip says "OK"; "list" in copy means the shopping list, and "Meals on your list" means every planned meal, recipe and saved meal that put something on it; "product" is "price" in copy (Kitchen's "Stores & prices", "Add a price"). A new word for an old concept, or an old word for a new one, is a finding; the design and product reviews grep new copy against this list.
- **Pinch follows the insight budget and the door rule in `CLAUDE.md` "Design & UX".** `src/apps/pinch/JOURNEYS.md` holds today's per-screen counts (§4.2), the doors per feature (§4.1) and the decisions behind them. A rule below that says a fact appears "wherever" something is shown means once per surface, in the figure, not on every row and every drawer; before adding a nudge, count, flag or entry point, list where the same fact or feature already shows. The measured checks for doors, front matter, control rows that look alike, the type at the stove, ticks and an All switch are in `CLAUDE.md` "Design & UX" and "Designing a mini-app's look"; run them on every Pinch PR that touches those surfaces.

- **Missing details appear only as in-context nudge lines.** A missing price, package size or nutrition value is one quiet line where the gap is owned (a recipe, the Calendar's period), naming the ingredient that weighs most ("Chicken thigh and 4 more need a price · Add prices", `rankGaps`), with a "Not now" that quiets it until reload (it writes nothing; dismissals stored before are still honoured) and a short fill-in sheet that steps through the biggest first, says where each is used, keeps the store picked on the row before and starts each size in the recipe's own unit. Never a to-do list, a badge, a required field or a setup step. A total says what it leaves out in its figure ("$5.20 so far", "$0.08+ per serving", "No price yet" when nothing is priced) and through one warning icon beside it (`LeftOutTip`, two sentences that tell a missing price from a size that can't be compared and say where to add them); an average or ratio from a partial total says so too ("Avg per meal so far").
- **Three layers, recipes name only the ingredient.** Family, ingredient, product. A recipe or meal refers to an ingredient id, never a store or product; prices live on products. A price form reads the price back in the unit the person cooks with before saving, through the cost math's own conversion, so a wrong unit or "each" shows at entry, and a unit price is said in one unit per ingredient (the default price's), so its places compare.
- **The nudge lives where the gap is owned, not in every drawer.** The recipe drawer carries "Add prices" under its Cost tile, after the steps (alone in the tile's place while nothing is priced; closing the drawer before the fill-in sheet opens), and marks each unpriced line "No price yet" in a partly priced recipe; the saved-meal, day and planned meal views keep only their cost and its warning (the saved meal's and the planned meal's Cost tile after the plate), which says to add prices from the plate's recipes (or in Kitchen for a plain ingredient); the meal builder is a full-screen subview, so it shows "Cost $0.08" with the warning icon, which opens its small help modal on a phone (the one overlay allowed over a subview) and a tooltip on a computer, and nothing else opens over it. A frozen day has no nudge, since a new price doesn't change it by itself, and its warning and tile say so once ("…had no price when the day passed. A price you add now counts from today on.", "Not priced" over "Fixed when the day passed"), and its rows show a dash; once a price would change it, the day's drawer offers "Price this day with today's prices" instead (the bullet on pricing a day again).
- **"Yours" is what you added, adjusted, priced or cook with.** Custom ingredients, adjusted catalog ones, ones with a product and ones a recipe, a saved meal or a planned day that isn't frozen yet uses; typing in the search looks through every ingredient, so a first-run kitchen never hears "nothing matches" for something the catalog has. Removing an in-use recipe, ingredient or store says it is taken off your lists, not erased, and a store the person adds back from the list comes back. The "Needs a price" and "Has a price" filters only look through Yours, and the filter panel says so in one line, so a count of "22 ingredients" never reads as the whole catalog; typing with Yours picked says "N found in all ingredients". Needs a price is Kitchen's batch home for prices: "Add prices" above its rows opens the fill-in sheet for what it shows, and Kitchen rows carry no "No price yet" line.
- **Kitchen's other lists are doors, and say what wants a look in words.** Kitchen's header names what the tab holds ("Your ingredients, fridge and freezer, and prices."). Fridge & freezer and Stores & prices are two `EntryTile`s side by side below the search and filters (a `nav` named "Also in Kitchen", no visible caption), each only once something is behind it, with no count; Fridge & freezer says in words under its name what wants a look ("2 to eat by tomorrow, 1 past its date"), never a bare dot or a pill, and the status counts only what the landing shows first (the subview opens on the place holding what is due first). They step aside while a filter or search narrows the list. Stores & prices is one list: prices grouped under their store, a store heading opens the store's sheet, a store with no prices shows its heading and "No prices yet", and + Add asks "A price" or "A store".
- **A new recipe asks how to start, with every way side by side, and each way is its own view.** A drawer on a phone, the page's own list from `sm` up (`MethodPicker`, rows only): From text, From a file ("A photo, screenshot or PDF"), From a link, then "Write it yourself" last and quieter. Picking one only picks: the text box, the file drop or the link field lives on its own screen (back raises the phone's drawer again, or returns to the list from `sm` up, and each says "Write it yourself instead"), never revealed under the list; the button reads "Fill in the recipe", and leaving a form that holds typed or read-in work asks Keep editing / Discard. The readings fill the real form for review and never save. Everything a recipe normally has is a visible section of the form, never a "+ Add X" chip, in this order: title, servings and times, description, photo, ingredients, steps, where it's from, how to keep it, nutrition (the section every recipe needs comes before the optional ones), and a footer note about an ingredient is a link to that row. Under the list of ways a quiet "Not now? Keep it as an idea" opens the idea sheet over the screen, and the text and link screens end in a quiet "Save as an idea" (no AI call) that swaps in the idea's own view, so the person pastes first and decides after. Nutrition shows what was calculated per serving for the metrics switched on in View options (one quiet line, "Calories and macros are off.", when none is), lets the person change any shown number and reset the shown ones to the calculated values; a number equal to the calculated one stays derived.
- **The recipe form's editors are the drawers allowed over a subview.** The form's basics are summary rows, not boxes (so is "Keeping it", below the steps): Title, Prep and cook and Description each show a small caption, the value (the description clamped to two lines) and a chevron, and open their editor (`SummaryEditor`: a drawer on a phone or a short screen, a popover under the row from `sm`, each ending in Done; Enter in a one-line field closes it and never saves the recipe, and Escape or the back gesture closes only the editor). Servings stays an inline stepper. A recipe written from scratch opens its title editor once by itself; one from a reading, and any existing recipe, opens with every row closed. A bad value (minutes that aren't whole, a text over its limit) shows in red on its row as well as in the editor, and the pinned footer says what to fix. Prep and cook are two number fields, "Prep time" and "Cook time", each with a visible "min" suffix, never "(minutes)" in a label. On a phone adding and editing an ingredient (search, then amount, unit and note, with a quiet "No amount (to taste, a handful…)" under the amount that hides the unit and leaves the note to say how much), a step (one text box) or the nutrition numbers (four small fields and "Reset to what we calculated") each happens in a drawer on top of the recipe form, ending in Done (and "Add another" while adding); a drawer holds one level, never opens another overlay, and from `sm` up a row opens in place. A screen's header carries the recipe's or meal's name as it is typed.
- **An ingredient group is a name on its lines.** `RecipeIngredient.group` is `string | null`, with no collection behind it (a line saved before it reads as null and every save writes the key; at most 40 characters through `cleanGroupName`, and two spellings that differ only in case or spacing are one group, a client-only cap since the rules can't afford a per-line check). Every surface orders lines through `groupIngredientLines`: ungrouped lines first with no heading, then each group in the order its first line appears under a `SectionDivider` heading; a recipe with no groups looks as it did. A row's editor ends with "Group" (a `PickOrCreate` with "New group", nothing preselected and "No group", behind "+ Put it in a group" until the recipe has one), a heading opens its own "Group" editor that renames it, merges it into a group of the same name (saying so first) or removes it with "Removed the group … · Undo", and a new line starts in the last group (an exception to nothing preselected, said in the search). The same ingredient may sit in several groups and nothing merges those lines (the shopping list sums them per unit); `matchStepIngredients` spreads an ingredient's groups across the steps that name it, and a line shown away from its heading names its group only when its ingredient is in more than one ("Soy sauce · For the sauce"). The reader keeps the recipe's own headings word for word and never invents one. A change that only reorganizes a recipe (moving lines between groups, renaming or removing a group, how it keeps) records no tweak; lines reordered inside one group still do.
- **Taking a row out of a form is undoable for a few seconds.** Removing an ingredient or step from the recipe form (the ✕, the trash, or "Remove" in a drawer) or an item from the meal builder's plate takes it out at once and floats "Removed Salt · Undo · 6" above the pinned footer (`UndoSnackbar` over `useUndoRemoval`, counting 6 to 1): Undo puts the row back where it was, one removal is pending at a time (a newer one makes the older final), and the removal stands when the count ends. Whole-record deletes (a recipe, meal, ingredient, store, product) keep their confirm dialogs.
- **The plan builder starts with the person's own things and asks the day with pills.** An empty plate shows "Your recent recipes and saved meals" (at most 12, most recently planned, cooked or added first, nothing preselected) under the one search, which finds saved meals, recipes and ingredients; no second search field. "Change" is a strip of days (Today, Tomorrow, five weekday names, "Other day…" for the date box) and the meal pills, and it opens already showing when the plan starts from a recipe or a saved meal. A new plan starts on the clock's meal today and dinner on other days, moved to the nearest main meal the day lacks. The primary is "Plan for today" / "Plan for Thu", and the toast says where it landed with a guarded View. The builder never offers "Save to Saved meals".
- **Nutrition is entered on the label's basis and stored per 100 g.** The ingredient form asks "Per [amount] [g | oz | serving]" above the four numbers, converts to `nutritionPer100g`, shows what it saved ("Saved as per 100 g: 🔥200") and refuses a blank or absurd number with one line. The serving option waits for a serving size that converts to grams. The ingredient drawer switches between per serving and per 100 g and hides the switch when both would show the same numbers.
- **Rows can hide their numbers, and start with the fewest.** Kitchen and Recipes/Saved meals have one View options control (an eye button, `ListViewControls` over the shared `ViewOptions`), and the Calendar header has the same eye (hidden until there is a recipe or a saved meal). A list's sheet starts with "Nutrition, everywhere" (the four nutrition switches every screen follows; there is no other settings screen and no gear), then that list's own rows (show prices, show calories and macros, the nutrition basis, remembered on the device per person), then "About the numbers"; the Calendar's has the first, then "On the calendar" with "Show stats" (the tile row under the summary line and in a day's drawer, off to start: off, a day's drawer has a "Stats for this day" row, drawn only when the day has more than its Total; a stored `showAverages` from before it is ignored, so everyone starts off; a nutrition switch turned on from this sheet turns nothing else on) and "Show prices" for the Week's meal rows only (`pinch:<uid>:view:calendar`; the summary line, the Week summary and the day drawer keep theirs), and the last. A list starts with prices on and calories and macros off (a choice already stored is kept); switching a number on from a list's sheet also turns that list's macros line on (not on the Calendar), and the macros switch is never disabled (a hint while every number is off). On Recipes and Saved meals a third switch, "Show what's in stock" (on to start), hides the fridge and freezer line on every row without touching the In stock filter or the drawers. Prices and macros are independent lines on a row, hiding one never changes a total, and the ingredient drawer's per serving / per 100 g switch is the same setting as the list's, so a row and its drawer never disagree. A row is as tall as its lines: a title-only ingredient row is about 44px, one with a price line about 60px, and a row with a leading tile or logo is as tall as the tile; never a `min-h` that leaves blank space under a lone title. `FamilyGroup` and the recipe list estimate their height from the lines that will show (price and nutrition), so the scrollbar doesn't jump when an option changes.
- **Every recipe reading discloses first.** The photo, text and link ways each open their own line ("An AI reads the picture and fills in the form. It isn't saved.") before anything is sent; a row the reader couldn't match keeps its amount, says "Not in your ingredients yet · tap to add or choose", offers up to three close names in its drawer above "Add as new ingredient" and "Pick from your ingredients", and the footer says why Add is disabled. A line the source doesn't measure ("salt to taste", "a handful of parsley") arrives with no amount and its words as the note, and is never a reason Add is disabled ("salt and pepper" splits into two lines only on a signal in the text, a to-taste or for-garnish tail or both halves salt or pepper kinds, so "macaroni and cheese" and "sweet and sour sauce" stay whole); the response schema makes every ingredient key required and nullable, so the model always answers the note.
- **A details drawer keeps its actions together, behind one ⋯ More.** The footer is Modify (secondary, left), a 40px ⋯ More and the one primary, the next step for that record now, which takes the leftover width (a recipe's is Plan it, or Start cooking when it is on today's plan and not yet cooked there; a saved meal's is Plan it; a planned meal's follows its day: Start cooking or Eat from fridge tonight, none ahead, cooked or past, when Modify (still secondary: nothing is filled when there is no next step) and ⋯ share the row, and a fixed past day, with neither, has one wide "⋯ More"; its Eat view with one box puts "Ate 2" in the footer as the one filled button). Every other action is a row of the More view, swapped in place with ‹ Back and keeping its consequence subtitle and its guards: a recipe's fridge and freezer row first (`StockRows`, opening Fridge & freezer for it), then Start cooking or Plan it (whichever isn't the primary; Start cooking only with a step), Mark as cooked, Add to shopping list and Put some away (not for a recipe never cooked, not bulk and not in stock); a saved meal's stock row, Add to shopping list and Put some away; a planned meal's Start cooking, Eat from fridge or freezer and Save to Saved meals, filtered by its day (`getPlannedMealOffer().more`: no Start cooking once that recipe is cooked or the day has passed, Eat from only today or yesterday and never for what it cooked or its own cook's boxes, Save to Saved meals only for 2+ items no saved meal holds, the row the primary repeats left out), then Remove from this day, last, red and on its own (`ActionRow isDestructive`) behind its confirm. The front is the subject: a recipe has its title with one 40px icon door on its line (🕘 Notes and history), then its source as a soft `LabelChip` pill ("From Mom's recipe cards ›", only with a source: it closes the drawer and shows the Recipes list narrowed to that source; no door to the Sources screen), the description in two lines with a cover as a 64px thumbnail that opens full width in place, one muted facts line (servings · total time · cost per serving with its warning), then Ingredients, Steps, Keeping it, the Cost tile with its price note under it (the note alone in the tile's place while nothing is priced) and the macro tiles; a saved meal has On the plate first, then its Cost tile (in the planned meal's words, with its warning) and its macros "For the plate"; a planned meal has its name as the view's heading, On the plate, where each recipe keeps its own "Mark as cooked" chip (the round tick and "Cooked · Not cooked" once marked), then its Cost tile and macros. 🕘 shows the Cooked row ("Cooked 4 times, last Oct 12", the round tick, which opens the history) and the whole notes journal. Each view keeps its scroll, the sheet never shrinks between views, an open door is tinted and closes on a second tap, Escape and back step out one view at a time and focus returns to what opened it. The front never repeats what the recipe's row showed before it opened (its stock line and due pill); the ingredient drawer's line gives every fact an emoji (✏️ for yours, 🍽️ for a serving that was set, never a default nobody chose, 🍲 for where it is used) and the family name its weight; its places show the price and the unit price in the default price's unit, and a form opened from it (Adjust, Modify, a price) returns to it.
- **Where a recipe came from is a `Source`, never `Recipe.source`.** A source is an id and a label (`sources`, named by `Recipe.sourceId`); `source` only says how a draft was made. Readers go through `getRecipeSource`, so a missing key, `null` and a deleted source all mean "no source", and deleting a source clears `sourceId` on its recipes in batches without touching their `updatedAt` (it versions the cover) and never deletes a recipe. The recipe form's optional "Where it's from" is a visible `PickOrCreate` after the steps, offering the sources a recipe uses (a typed label still reuses any source with that name, ignoring case) and, for a recipe read from a link, starts on the site without taking focus. A source is a way to its recipes (the drawer's pill shows that source's recipes), and the way to the whole collection is the Recipes screen's, never a recipe's drawer: the header's Sources icon (`BookOpen`, a quiet 40px button beside "New recipe", only in the Recipes view once a source exists) opens the Sources subview, where a source with recipes is a row that shows them ("Show the N recipes from X", which closes the screen) and a source on no recipe is a plain row ("Not on any recipe", no chevron) with its trash, every row ending in a pencil that renames or deletes it; the Recipes filter (a `FilterBar` with one Source question, pills with counts, "No source · n" only when some recipe has none) appears once a source exists, with no link of its own. Sources are made only in the recipe form. A failed sources listener never reaches the load-error screen.
- **The shopping list is one line per ingredient and unit, filled from a sheet that picks what goes on it.** An item is `shoppingItems/{ingredientId}__{unit}`, so adding the same thing again merges: an unchecked line gains the amount (two decimals), a checked one starts again unchecked, a missing one is created, all in one `runTransaction` that reads every target first; units are never converted. Each item keeps `sources` (planned meal ids, `recipe:<id>:<servings>` with the servings the add put on the list, summed when the same recipe is added again onto an open line and compared by `parseShoppingSource`'s key without them, an older `recipe:<id>` read as the recipe's own servings, `meal:<id>`; `[]` typed; key missing on old lines, read `?? []`), merged from the transaction's own read and capped at 60; ticks and amount edits never touch it, a unit move carries it, Clear and remove forget it with the document. A recipe line with no amount is a name-only line (amount null, EACH): null + x = x, a batch drops it when the ingredient has an amount in any unit, and the list and the add sheet draw one inside that ingredient's amount row ("Salt" is one row, not two); a name-only line an amount absorbs hands its sources to that amount. Lines come from the pure `utils/shopping.ts` (a recipe scaled by servings over its own; a meal, planned meal or day: recipe items by their servings, ingredient items at their serving size) and are checked by `npm run check:pinch-math`. Ticking (a `writeBatch` over a row's items), changing and removing are field-scoped writes that touch only their own row (no sheet-wide busy); removing a line and clearing what you got take effect at once with an Undo toast (no confirm), and Undo recreates each item as it was unless it is back on the list; "Clear" is one `runTransaction` per chunk of 250 that re-reads each item and deletes only those still ticked (an item another device un-ticked survives) and returns what it really cleared, for its Undo; and the 200 lines per add and the 300-item soft cap are the app's limits, not the rules'. Tapping a row's name ticks it (the amount opens from a 40×40 chevron button). A tick holds its row for 1.2 s (`SHOPPING_MOVE_DELAY_MS`): the write, the tab badge and the cost follow at once, but the row stays where it was drawn, struck through, before it moves to the Got it half (an un-tick leaves it the same way), so the rows around it never shift under a second tap; each row has its own timer, the held rows sit in a ref that renders nothing when a row is held (only letting go renders), timers end with the screen, and "Clear" works on what is stored. A ticked line that changes unit stays ticked, and moving into a unit already on the list adds to an open line or restarts a ticked one, which the row sheet says before saving. The recipe and saved meal drawers carry "Add to shopping list" as a row of their ⋯ More, and the day drawer a tinted "Add to shopping list" row after its meals that says how much of the day is already on the list (a planned meal shops through its day), not on a day that has passed, that closes the drawer and opens `AddToShoppingSheet` (titled "Shopping list", the verb is on the row and the button; it also takes a `{ kind: 'range' }` of days, and the Shopping tab's "+ Add" opens the same body as "From your plan": the next seven days, "Change" for a range calendar, days before today left out): it says "Untick what you already have" (or "Tick what you need" when nothing starts ticked), notes what is already put away (naming at most three recipes, then "and N more") and says "Adding 3 of 6", a recipe gets a servings stepper, one row per ingredient and kind of unit, a row starts unticked only when this sheet's own sources already put it on the list ("Already on your list for Thu dinner"), adds only the share not yet there when some of its sources did ("; this adds the rest"), and starts ticked when something else put it there ("On your list · 2 lb"); an old line with no sources key keeps the unticked guard; the day drawer's row reads "On your list ✓" once every planned meal of the day is a source, else counts the rows its sheet starts unticked; and the staples under "Usually at home: tick what you're out of" (spices, oils, vinegar, salt, water), one scrolling list sits under a fixed header (with a floor of about three rows on a phone under 800px high), and a toast says what was added with a "View" button. The list is the fourth tab (`ShoppingScreen`, no back button): in shop sections in walking order (`SHOP_SECTION_BY_FAMILY`, dividers only from 8 rows; rows mount in chunks of 12 near the viewport, a section draws 100 rows then "Show N more", two columns from `lg`), amounts read as things to pick up (a count rounds up, a spice or oil under a tablespoon shows its name only, one ingredient's two units are one row), under a thin To buy · n / Got it · n / All · n switch (the counts are rows, the unit of the rows beneath them): the halves show one at a time and All shows what is left, then the got rows under a "Got it" divider, struck through, in the same list (counts follow the search, the shown view is derived, from a half a search that matches only the other half lands there and All stays All, "Clear what you got" lives in the Got it half and on All's divider, only while something is got and never while searching) and a search from 8 rows; the row's one detail line names what a line is for and never counts ("2 lb · for Thu dinner and Adobo chicken": a planned meal by its slot, its dish added only when two plates share the slot, recipes and saved meals by name, soonest first, three in full, then two and "and N more", `joinSourceNames`), wrapping rather than cutting a name (the chunk estimate counts the wrapped lines), its sheet lists every one with its share (five, then "Show N more" when four or more would hide; shares in the row's unit rounded by largest remainder so they add up to its amount), and a source that is gone is dropped; its row and add sheets are ordinary `FormSheet`s over the tab. Under the search, once a meal put something on the list and never while searching, the "Meals on your list" tile ("For Fri dinner, Fri lunch and 20 more") opens `ShoppingMealsSheet`: every meal soonest first with what is left to buy ("3 of 8 to buy", "Got everything"), a search from 8, and a quiet Remove while something is left to buy. Remove (`stopShoppingFor`, one `runTransaction` per chunk over the pure `planStopShopping`) takes that meal's share off, worked out from what it added (a recipe at the servings in its tag; a planned or saved meal as it is now, since it has no stepper), keeps another meal's share, ticked lines and typed lines, leaves its row in place struck through ("Taken off your list"), and raises a toast that counts drawn rows ("7 things came off your list", what went down, what stays because something else still needs it) with an Undo that restores only lines still as it left them (`isAsStopLeft`); a remainder on a line it was the only source of may be an amount the person typed, so it stays, untagged, and the toast says it went down; it doesn't start offline, the modal from `sm` opens on Done, the names don't open the meal (that would be an overlay on an overlay), and what can drift (a planned or saved meal edited or added twice since, a deleted planned meal that can't be taken off) is in TECHNICAL.md. Under the search, a cost line says what it covers ("About $3.16 for 3 of 4 things") with a help icon (a warning when it leaves something out and names it), only when it has a figure (nothing under half priced or with nothing priced, so Shopping never says "Not enough prices yet" or "No price yet"; it sits under the search so the field doesn't move between To buy and Got it): it prices the amounts from default products, not packages, so the till total is usually higher. The add toast's "View" switches to the tab only when no subview is open, otherwise it only dismisses, and both add sheets wait for the shopping listener (`isLoaded`, no `loadError`) before they add. A failed shopping listener logs, clears its items and degrades only its own screen and sheets. The one-thing add sheet stays open after a pick ("Added Whole milk", Done) and its search ranks an exact name or alias first, then a name's start, then a catalog family's members.

- **A recipe idea is a link, a photo or a few words, kept until it becomes a recipe.** It is the third pill on Recipes (Recipes, Saved meals, Ideas; a pill shows once it has something: Saved meals with a saved meal or a second recipe, Ideas with an idea or a load error), and the header then reads Ideas with "New idea". `ideas/{id}` holds `kind` (LINK, PHOTO, TEXT), title, note, url, siteName, imageUrl, photoPath and `recipeId`; the picture address is https only and a third party's, so it loads only through `FallbackImage` with the kind's tile (🔗 📷 📝) as the fallback. "New idea" is one `FormSheet` that swaps the `MethodPicker` list of ways for a way's own view with a "Back" link, never a second overlay. A link says what is fetched before anything is sent ("We fetch the page to find its title and picture. Nothing is saved from it except those."), is looked up through `fetchPageContent` for `meta` only (six seconds, a failure never cached as an answer), and saving waits for it to settle (Save is off with a footer note, six seconds at most), so a link is named after its page or the person is asked for a title: a failed, slow or title-less lookup shows the Title field, and a title left blank saves with the host. A link or a few words then close the sheet as soon as the save is checked and written on the phone, and a row whose save hasn't reached the server after a moment says "Saves when you're back online"; a photo waits for its upload, with Cancel turned into Close and a line saying why. A link already on the list (`getComparableUrl`) opens that idea instead of saving a copy. The drawer's one primary is "Turn it into a recipe" (a link idea opens the recipe start's link way with its address already filled in, nothing sent until the person taps, and the reading fills the form for review keeping the idea's own title and note; "Write it yourself instead", a photo and a few words open the form with the title, the note as the description and the link's host as the source, and no line repeating the idea's title (the link way's reading screen keeps "From your idea: …" above it; a photo idea's form keeps one line about its photo); the recipe commits first on its own and the idea's `recipeId` is set by a separate write right after, whichever way the form was reached, whose failure is logged and never loses the recipe; a photo isn't copied and the form says so) or "Open the recipe" once made. A deleted or archived recipe reads as "not made yet", nothing cascades, the 200-idea cap is the app's and not the rules', and a failed ideas listener degrades only its own list ("New idea" stays on screen but disabled until the ideas have loaded, and `createIdea` refuses too). A save that fails says why as one red line in the pinned footer's `note`, and it clears when the form changes.
- **Cooking mode is one session of a recipe or a planned plate, one step at a time, at each recipe as written, and Finish records the cooks.** "Start cooking" is a row of the recipe drawer's ⋯ More (only with a step), or the drawer's primary when the recipe is on today's plan and not yet cooked there (then it carries that meal's servings and id, so Finish marks that meal's cook), and in the planned meal view (tonight's primary unless a due box makes Eat from fridge the primary, a ⋯ More row on a day ahead or while that box is the primary, never on a day that has passed or for a recipe already cooked for that meal; a plate with one recipe still to cook opens it, and two or more open one session holding all of them (`getPlateCookRecipes`; never a chooser)). It closes the drawer and opens an overlay `Subview` (`kind: 'cook'`) whose header back, Escape and back gesture share one `leave()`: it closes at once, or asks "Stop timers and leave?" (Stay / Leave, naming how many) while a timer is running or paused, with an "Ingredients" button beside the step counter ("Step 2 of 7" and a progress bar that shrinks, never dots; from the ingredient list the header back, Escape and the back gesture return to the steps first; from `lg` the two sit side by side, no button, the step's lines tinted in the list); a plate's recipes are `CookDishSwitch` cards that say each one's step (names wrap to two lines), never pills, under a header named by the plan's own name or `getPlateTitle` of its recipes, each recipe keeping its own step, ticks and servings, with "Next: {recipe}" on a recipe's last step and Finish only once every recipe is on its last: the step in 28px (30 from `lg`, a size smaller below 640px tall and past 160 and 400 characters), its ready timer cards (Start only), then a quieter tinted "For this step" block 24px below a card or 32px below the step, of the lines it is first to name with their amounts (`matchStepIngredients`, once per recipe), Back and Next 56px tall and pinned (a compact row on a short landscape screen) with the timers in the background as one 40px row of pills above them that scrolls sideways (each pill one button, only the time left and the step's first words, a tap bringing it into focus; beside Back and Next on a short landscape screen), swipe and arrow keys, Finish on the last step. It starts at the recipe's own servings (`getCookStartServings`; a plan's count only when it asks for more), a plan's count is "You planned 2 for tonight" and what the put-away counts as eaten, and the steppers move a whole serving a tap (a half only below one). Amounts scale through `scaleAmount`, the shopping list's own math, and read as kitchen measures (`formatKitchenAmount`: fractions, a sliver of a cup in tbsp, whole items with "about"; display only); a line with no amount shows its note ("to taste") and never scales. Finish records the cook (started from a planned meal it marks that meal's own cook, and one that already exists takes the servings made instead; a plate finishes once: every recipe's cook in one transaction by `markPlannedPlateCooked`, the plan's own cook per recipe so one already marked is never doubled, and one Undo for all of them by `removeCooks`, one batch) and swaps in one centered panel of framed cards: "Nice work", the record card (Marked as cooked, its own guarded Undo until Done or until a box is put away or a note saved from the panel, Servings made saved on the cook, one stepper per recipe on a plate), the put-away card (one per bulk recipe, with the recipe's name above it) and "Add a note" (one row per recipe, typed in place, Cancel and Save note in the footer, "Note saved." after, never closing the screen), with one Done that ignores a tap right after Finish; nothing in cooking mode toasts, timers run on until Done asks, and leaving before Finish writes nothing. Finish only records while the cooks listener has landed without error, else it leaves as before. When the recipe has notes, a plain muted line with a chevron above the step (a 40px tap area, no fill or border) (not on the final panel) says "📝 Oct 12: …" ("Your latest note" for a screen reader; the latest NOTE, leading with its "Next time…" sentence, "You've changed the recipe since." when a tweak followed), a tap opens the notes in place, never a sheet over the screen, and a note's "Apply to the recipe" leaves through the same checks. Times in a step (`findDurations`, a general util) become ready timer cards on the step (`CookStepTimer`, a ready card only: the first four times with no timer yet, one tap to start, never started on their own; `getReadyStepTimers` leaves out a time that already has one), up to four live timers for the whole session, named by the step's first words (and by the recipe on a plate; running or paused; a finished one waits for Dismiss and doesn't count) running to a clock deadline. Start makes the timer the screen (`CookTimerView`: "Step 1 of 3 · Show this step", which opens the step and its amounts in place; on a plate the dish; the timer's name; the time left sized to the card (`cqi`, 88px at 390, 72px at 320, "1:30:00" smaller) with a progress bar; the other timers as rows that each become the big one on a tap, with their own Pause, Resume or Dismiss, and any other time on the step with Start; "Up next" with the next step's first sentence; two columns under 500px tall, one centred column from `lg`), with one wide primary in the footer (Pause, a running timer's only control, then Resume with Reset as a quiet link under the bar, then Dismiss) beside "Next", which leaves it running; the note line, dish cards, step text and Ingredients button are gone while it waits. Back, Escape, the back gesture and a swipe right put it in the background and return to the step that was showing. A finished timer comes into focus by itself (an accent card, a bell, "Time's up" in big type) except over a note being typed or a put-away; the one that rang first stays in front ("Rang 2 min ago", ringing again about once a minute, up to five times), its Dismiss returns to where the person was, its Next goes on (and isn't drawn when the person is already on that step), and going back leaves it waiting as a lit pill; a dismissed one leaves "✓ Done · 30 min" with "Start again" on its step card. On a plate the wait offers "Meanwhile: <other dish> · Step 1 of 2", one tap to start the other dish. Focus is `useCookTimers().focused`, its transitions pure and checked (`getFocusedTimerId`, `getFocusAfterFinish`, `getFocusAfterDismiss`). A buzz and a beep fail quietly, and a toast shows only while the screen is hidden or covered; leaving ends the timers, and at the foot of the timer view, only while its timer runs, one line says "Keep this screen open: timers stop if you leave it." (never on every step or in the pinned footer). A recipe changed or removed elsewhere keeps the session going on what it last had, with one quiet line saying so. `useWakeLock` keeps the screen on and, only when it can't, that line at the foot of the timer view becomes "This device may turn the screen off; timers keep running only while this screen is open." Its only writes are that cook (and its servings), what is put away and a note: no other Firestore, indexes, Storage or `localStorage`. No cost or nutrition is shown at the stove.

- **A cook is a quiet record that a recipe was made.** `cooks/{id}` holds `recipeId`, `plannedMealId`, `servings`, `cookedAt` (an instant, shown in local time) and the two times, owner only, one document each. The ways in are the "Mark as cooked" row of the recipe drawer's ⋯ More (one tap at the recipe's own servings and a toast "Marked Adobo chicken as cooked" with an Undo that deletes exactly that cook; the drawer's 🕘 Notes and history then starts with a "Cooked 3 times, last Oct 12" row with the round tick that opens the history) and, on today or a day that has passed, a "Mark as cooked" chip on each recipe's item in a planned meal (now for today, local noon of that day for a past one; the id `{plannedMealId}__{recipeId}` and a `runTransaction` make a second mark "Already marked", and the item then reads "Cooked · Not cooked" after the round tick, which asks first ("Not cooked after all?", naming the recipe) because it can come weeks later, and cooking mode started from that meal finishes into the same cook, or writes the servings made onto it when it already exists; once every recipe of a meal is cooked, the day drawer shows the soft round tick beside its name, today or behind, never ahead). The Recipes list doesn't show a cook count (nothing on it sorts or filters by it); the drawer does. Deleting a recipe's confirm names its cooking history (how many times) and its notes, and the idea it was made from going back to the ideas. The history is a `FormSheet` whose rows open one cook's day, time and servings in place (a "Back" link, a field-scoped `updateDoc`, an icon-only trash with a destructive confirm that names the day) and "+ Add an earlier cook"; it draws 8 rows and "Show N more" only when more than three would hide. The 500-cooks-per-recipe cap is the app's, not the rules'; a failed cooks listener degrades only its own UI (no row, no line); archiving a recipe keeps its cooks and a hard delete finds them with a query on the recipe (the store can be empty) and removes them in batches, best effort, since every reader ignores a cook whose recipe is gone. Toasts sit above drawers (`index.css`), so an Undo raised from one can be tapped. A planned meal's mark is a transaction, which needs a connection, so a failed cook write says "Check your connection and try again."; the drawer's "Mark as cooked" row is disabled until its write settles, cooking mode's Finish records once (its Undo runs once, in the panel, and takes back every cook the screen wrote or none, and its Done ignores a tap that lands right after Finish), and a write that resolves late never closes a screen it didn't open (`closeSubviewIf`).
- **A recipe's notes are a journal, and a tweak is the dated record of an edit.** `notes/{id}` holds `recipeId`, `kind` (NOTE or TWEAK), `text`, `changes`, `cookId` and the two times, owner only; a NOTE is the person's words (always `text`, optionally tied to the cook it follows, and a deleted cook leaves a plain note), a TWEAK is written by `saveRecipe` in the recipe's own `writeBatch` when the recipe has a cook and the edit changed what the form edits (never a new recipe, a never-cooked one, a cover-only edit or while the cooks or notes listener hasn't landed), its `changes` computed at save time by the pure `getRecipeChanges` (at most 8 plain lines, "and N more" last) and immutable, its `text` the optional "What changed and why?" line. `Recipe` has no field for it: the newest TWEAK is the recipe's last change, which its own entry dates ("Changed on Oct 20"; the drawer's front names no tweak), and a NOTE older than it says "Written before your Oct 20 tweak". Past notes are on demand, never on the drawer's front: the "Notes" section lives in the drawer's 🕘 Notes and history view under the Cooked row, and its heading counts its entries only past ten or while some are folded (one "Add a note" row while empty; then the row, the entries newest first, a TWEAK's heading "Changed on Oct 20" beside a small "Tweak" tag, five shown and "Show N more" only when more than three would hide, text clamped at four lines with "More"); "Add a note" and Edit close the drawer and open the `FormSheet` "Note" (the words, and "Is this about a time you cooked it?" as pills only for a cooked recipe and only when the note wasn't started from a cook, starting on a cook from today, "Today"; the trash with a destructive confirm). A NOTE entry (the drawer's and cooking mode's) has "Apply to the recipe", which opens the recipe form with the note quoted and a new TWEAK on save, the NOTE untouched. Each cook in the history that has no note has an "Add a note" that swaps in place (below Day, Time and Servings in its own view), and cooking mode's last screen offers "Add a note" typed in place, never a sheet over the subview. An edit saves only `text` and `updatedAt`; an add writes a fresh id with `setDoc`; both wait for the notes listener (`isLoaded`, no `loadError`) and a close that follows an awaited write (the sheet, the history's note view, the cooking screen) is a functional update on its own target, so a late save never closes what the person has opened since; a hard delete reads the recipe's notes from Firestore (the store is empty while they load) and removes them in batches, best effort, and an archive keeps them; the 300 per recipe is the app's cap, not the rules'; a failed notes listener logs, clears its items and takes away only the Notes section's add row (the recipe still saves, without a tweak).
- **A recipe's care is one optional row, one drawer section and one line.** `Recipe.care` is `{ fridgeDays, freezerDays, reheat, tip } | null` (days whole, 1 to 365; reheat and tip at most 300 characters each), written by every save of the recipe, so a recipe from before it (no key) gains it as null, and read through `getRecipeCare`, which treats a missing key, null and a map of nothing alike. The form's "Keeping it" row sits after "Where it's from" and before Nutrition (`RecipeCareField`, a `SummaryEditor`: two "days" fields, a reheating line and a tip, small captions and 40px fields; its summary reads "Fridge 3 days, freezer 3 months, reheating, tip", joined with commas so a wrap never leaves a dot at a line's end; days are typed as days and shown as weeks or months when they fit, a month being 30). The drawer's "Keeping it" section (🥛 ❄️ ♨️ 💡 lines in a 20px emoji column, the reheat one never 🔥, which is calories) sits between Steps and Notes and exists only when there is something to say, and cooking mode's put-away pills carry the times ("Fridge · keeps 3 days", "Freezer · keeps 3 months"). The three readings fill it for review from what the source states and never an estimate, a range as its shorter end (a safety figure, unlike a cooking timer's longer end), weeks and months as days rounded down, anything outside 1 to 365 dropped; a reading with none leaves it null and adds nothing to the "couldn't read" list. A change to it never records a tweak (storage advice isn't a change to the dish, and a tweak would move the "changed" date and relabel older notes), and Pinch has no copy-out, so nothing carries it away.

- **The fridge and freezer list is containers: one document per physical box, owner only, kept until finished.** `containers/{id}` (a `Container`) holds `title`, `recipeId` / `mealId` / `cookId` (immutable, never a recipe and a meal together), `servings` (whole portions, 1 to 100), `status` (`IN_STOCK` or `DONE`), `place` (`FRIDGE` or `FREEZER`), `eatBy` and a `history` of at most 10 events (MADE, FRIDGE, FREEZE, THAW, EAT, TOSS, EDIT; the rules can only walk a list by index and the evaluator stops at 1,000 expressions, so a longer one drops the oldest EAT first, then the oldest EDIT, then, in a long run of moves, the oldest thaw after the first place event; what went in and every freeze stay). A container is never split (a put-away of portions in separate boxes writes one to twenty containers in one batch, each its own history): eating some lowers `servings`, the last portion or a toss sets `DONE` and keeps the document as history, and Delete is its own destructive action that says the history goes with it. `eatBy` is a date-only value (UTC midnight, `fromDateInputValue`, shown with the planned-day helpers); "Eat soon" is due today or tomorrow in the viewer's local time and "Past its date" is before today, each shown as the row's one eat-by item in a soft pill ("Eat today", "Eat by tomorrow", "Past its date") and plain words otherwise (a row says one date once, never a date and a "soon" word side by side); event times are instants. Every change that depends on the container's own state is a `runTransaction` over a pure plan in `utils/containers.ts` and says in one plain sentence when it can't happen. The default eat-by comes from the recipe's `care` or a named default, is shown as the person's own call ("Your call"), and no copy says food is safe. A move starts from the date the container already has: past its date stays past through any move and the view says so, a thaw never starts later than it, and a refreeze says it has been frozen before. Only `IN_STOCK` is listened to (`startContainersListener`, from `usePinchSync`, an optional extra: its failure logs, clears the list and shows one line on its own surfaces, never the load-error screen); Finished is read on demand through TanStack Query (the `status` + `updatedAt` index); scoped to one recipe or meal it reads that recipe's or meal's own containers (one equality, at most 200), so an older finished one is never hidden behind the newest 25. A saved meal's stock counts whole plates, its own boxes plus the dish with the fewest in that place (`getMealStockMap`), and a recipe whose only use is in-stock containers is archived, not erased. Stock shows as `StockLine` on a recipe or meal row, in words ("🥛 5 in the fridge"; 🥛 fridge, ❄️ freezer), and as `StockRows` at the top of its drawer's ⋯ More: one row with a line per place ("🥛 5 servings in the fridge [Eat by tomorrow]", "❄️ 5 servings in the freezer"), a saved meal's sources under them, opening Fridge & freezer for it, above "Put some away"; a planned meal eats from a box through its primary or its More's "Eat from fridge/freezer" row; and Recipes and Saved meals have an "In stock" filter that says so on its active chip. Cooking mode asks "Putting any away?" only for a bulk meal (`isBulkMeal`: five or more servings, a recipe that says it freezes, or one already in stock) that has something left after tonight (the plan's count, else 2) and what this cook already put away, and otherwise shows the same card as "Put some away" with the two place pills (each carrying its keeping time), "Put another away" only while something is left; nothing is written until Save (which never holds the screen waiting for the server), a note saved first keeps the question, and the containers carry the `cookId`. The Finish panel is one centered column of framed cards (the record card, the question, a card of settings rows with each label on the left and its stepper or date on the right, and a confirmation card with a check, what was saved, the eat-by date and its own Undo), never a left-aligned stack floating in a centered page; the panel confirms itself, so a put-away from it raises no toast over the "Marked as cooked" one. Every container action and every Undo ignores a second tap (an Undo runs once per toast), and a box's sheet opens with focus on Done (or the drawer), never on an action. The sheet, titled with the dish, asks two things: one big "Ate one" that closes it with "Ate 1 · 4 left · Undo", and "It's gone" (Ate it / Tossed, no confirm: the Undo is the net); freeze or thaw stays, the date line edits the date, and "How many are left?" is the one count (fewer is an eat, more a correction). It never scrolls at 390×844 or 320×568; the history is one tap away. Boxes put away together are one row ("3 boxes of 2 servings", a display grouping by moment, place, eat-by and dish: a box moved or re-dated alone leaves it), whose sheet eats "a box" at a time and ends, re-dates or deletes the batch in one write. The list shows one place at a time: a thin switch of Fridge and Freezer counted in servings ("Fridge · 10 servings"; counts follow the scope chip and the search, the shown place is derived each render (before any pick the place holding what is due first, the fridge when nothing is due) and falls to the other place while a search matches only there, both places keep their option when empty), so a full fridge and a full freezer never mean scrolling past one to reach the other. "What you finished" is a quiet link under the list that opens its own step (no Add there). Each place has its bulk end, "Clear out the fridge/freezer", on a line under the switch and only while no scope chip or search narrows the list: a destructive confirm that says it keeps them in What you finished as cleared out, one `runTransaction` per 200 containers that re-reads each and ends only those still in that place (a `CLEAR` history event, an end event like `EAT` and `TOSS`), a count of what it really cleared, and an Undo that puts back only what is still as the clear-out left it; any finished box's sheet offers "Put it back" while what ended it is still its last event. A freezer row leads with when it went in ("Frozen Oct 5") and names its eat-by only within a week or past. A read of what you finished that only reached an empty cache says it couldn't load, never "nothing". Fridge & freezer lives under Kitchen: no Calendar or Overview surface of its own and no push for an eat-by date.


- **A passed day is priced again only when the person asks, and nothing else about it changes.** Its meals keep the `snapshot` the app froze them with; "Price this day with today's prices" is the one thing that replaces it. It is a tinted `ActionRow` in the day drawer (no help icon: its confirm previews the result), shown only for a day that has passed, with the kitchen loaded, when today's prices would change a total, a line or what it leaves out (`wouldRepriceChange`, never for today, a day ahead, an unchanged or empty day). Its subtitle and confirm say it redoes the day's cost and nutrition from today's prices and recipes (a changed recipe can move the day, calories included), true even for a day that had no prices. It asks first with a destructive confirm that previews the result ("Before" in the cost tile's words and "After" as "about $0.66", one figure per line, and how many ingredients still have no price only above zero, worked out at the tap by `getRepricePreview` with the function the write uses) and says it can't be undone ("Use today's prices for Oct 12?", no Undo), then one `runTransaction` per day (`repriceDay`) re-reads each meal and replaces only `snapshot` and `updatedAt`, so planned meal ids, and the cooks that hang off them, stay; the row is disabled until it settles, a failure is one plain sentence under it, and a toast says "Oct 12 now uses today's prices". `snapshot.repricedAt` (null when the app froze the day, an instant when the person asked; older snapshots lack the key and read as null) is what the rules require to replace a snapshot and what the copy reads: "Fixed when the day passed" until then and "Priced with today's prices on Oct 14" after, under a tile that reads "Not priced" when nothing could be priced, never "as they were that day". The app's own freezing never touches a snapshot that exists.
- **Back closes the top layer, and each tab keeps its place.** Every drawer, sheet and "‹ Back" step takes the back gesture one layer at a time (`DetailSheet`/`FormSheet` do it; a swapped-in view calls `useBackStep`; a `HelpTip` modal is a layer too, so back on a tab closes the help note instead of leaving the tab, and a reload with layers open costs no extra press); back from any tab returns to the Calendar and from the Calendar leaves Pinch; a tab's scroll, pill, search and period live in the session (`usePinchSessionState`), never in a view that unmounts. Tab icons: Calendar 📅 `CalendarDays`, Recipes `ChefHat`, Kitchen `Refrigerator`, Shopping `ShoppingBasket`; "cooked" actions use `CircleCheck` and a done cook shows the round `TickMark`, never a tab's icon.
- **State the person expects back after switching views lives in the session, not in a conditionally rendered view.** Cooking mode's ticks, step and servings sit in `CookingSession`, one entry per recipe of the plate, beside the timers, so going to Ingredients and back, or to another recipe and back, keeps them, and they end with the screen; a view that unmounts keeps nothing of its own that the person would miss. A tab kept mounted under a subview is changed by an announcement it listens for (`announceSourceShown`/`useOnSourceShown`, `announceRecipeAdded`), never by the subview writing session state: subviews render outside `PinchSessionContext`, so their `usePinchSessionState` reaches nothing.
- **A stored picture's cache version is a field the picture owns.** A download URL is cached by path and a version; when the version is an `updatedAt` that any edit touches, `useStorageImageUrl` keeps the previous picture on screen for the same path while the new one loads, so editing a note never flashes the thumbnail to its placeholder.

- **Vendored assets keep their licence.** Pinch vendors nothing right now (the ingredient icons were removed); a store logo comes from Logo.dev and is credited in "About the numbers", the last line of every View options sheet. Add any new vendored set with its notice beside it.
- **Check lists at scale.** Pinch needs an oversized seed fixture like Waypoint's (`scripts/seeds/pinchScale.ts`, "Big Kitchen (scale test)"). Open new lists on it at phone width with the dev build throttled, and keep per-row work cheap (CLAUDE.md "Performance is a design check"): catalog groups mount only near the viewport (`LazyMount` plus `defer-offscreen`), and a long list (Stores & prices, a week's agenda) caps its rows with "Show N more".
